mission: Classify the emergent strategic functions of relationships among cyberattack activities, rather than merely listing their individual technical mechanisms, to enable evidence-based defensive reasoning by humans and AI systems.

principles.rule: The primary classification unit is a repeatable strategic composition of at least two distinct adversarial activities; an isolated technique, vulnerability, alert or indicator is not a composition.
A composition class identifies the functional relationship and emergent strategic property, not merely a sequence, simultaneous events, or a list of techniques.
Temporal association, functional effect, causal dependency, actor attribution and strategic intent are separate claims. Timing alone never establishes coordination or intent.
Classify with public evidence, explicit uncertainty, alternative explanations, exclusion criteria and independent review. Novelty is a hypothesis until checked against prior art.
Provide persistent identifiers, versioned definitions, public machine-readable representations and traceable evidence. Preserve history and distinguish proposed classes from accepted classes.
Enable humans and AI to read, challenge and propose revisions; no autonomous acceptance or governance changes. The repository owner retains final authority.

Remain a defensive classification knowledge base complementing existing standards. Detection engines, websites, APIs and integrations are subordinate to the taxonomy; no offensive operational guidance.

amendment_policy: No ordinary change may alter this charter or foundational invariants. A separate public amendment proposal, explicit repository-owner approval and documented rationale are required. Preserve all prior versions; no AI agent may approve an amendment.
